scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a config-cleanup window, a user on pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) reports they
lost all reach across the fabric -- pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) is unreachable,
though pc_0_1 can still ping its own gateway 10.0.1.1. Both spine
routers report their BGP session toward leaf_router_0_1 down at the
same time, yet leaf_router_0_1's uplink interfaces show UP and its FRR
daemons are all running. Investigate.

injection.action: delete both spine neighbor statements from the running BGP config

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_1 BGP neighbor configuration
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_1 (AS 65201) normally peers with
  spine_router_0_0 (neighbor 172.16.0.6 remote-as 65100) and
  spine_router_0_1 (neighbor 172.16.0.10 remote-as 65101). Both
  neighbor statements were deleted from the running config, so bgpd
  sends a Cease notification and drops both sessions. With zero peers
  the leaf stops advertising 10.0.1.0/24 (the spines withdraw it
  immediately) and stops learning 10.0.0.0/24, so pc_0_1 is isolated
  even though bgpd is running and every link is UP.
Localization: leaf_router_0_1
Root cause: both BGP neighbor statements removed under
  `router bgp 65201` on leaf_router_0_1
Fix: re-add the two neighbor statements on leaf_router_0_1 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
Re-add the spine neighbors on leaf_router_0_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 65201"
 -c "neighbor 172.16.0.6 remote-as 65100"
 -c "neighbor 172.16.0.10 remote-as 65101"`
Note: the injection changed only the running config; the intended
config is still intact in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so `service frr restart`
on leaf_router_0_1 is an equally correct fix (it reloads the file and
re-creates both neighbors).
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: BGP neighbor configuration removed / no configured peers
must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: uplink interfaces UP and bgpd running while both spine sessions are down -- a config fault, not a link or daemon fault
bonus-cites-missing-neighbors: names the missing neighbor statements (172.16.0.6 / spine_router_0_0 and 172.16.0.10 / spine_router_0_1) or shows `show bgp summary` with zero peers

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is the BGP neighbor configuration inside the FRR
`bgpd` process on leaf_router_0_1. During the config-cleanup window, all
`neighbor` statements were accidentally removed from that router's running
configuration, while every other element (ASN 65201, router-id 172.16.0.7,
and the `network 10.0.1.0/24` advertisement) was left intact.

Because leaf_router_0_1 has no neighbors declared, FRR never initiates or
accepts a BGP TCP session on port 179. Both spine routers (spine_router_0_0
and spine_router_0_1) still have leaf_router_0_1 configured as a peer
(172.16.0.7 and 172.16.0.11 respectively), so they continuously attempt
connections and cycle in the "Active" state — confirmed by `show bgp summary`
on both spines. The `show bgp summary` run directly on leaf_router_0_1
returned `% No BGP neighbors found in VRF default`, providing direct proof.

Because no BGP session is ever established, 10.0.1.0/24 is never advertised
into the fabric. No spine or super-spine learns a return path to pc_0_1, so
all cross-fabric traffic (including pc_0_0 ↔ pc_0_1) is black-holed. pc_0_1
can still ping its own gateway (10.0.1.1 on leaf_router_0_1 eth2) because
that is a locally connected route, requiring no BGP — matching the reported
symptom exactly.

Root cause: the BGP neighbor declarations were stripped from leaf_router_0_1
during the cleanup, leaving the router BGP-isolated despite healthy physical
uplinks.

Corrective fix: re-add the two missing neighbor statements to leaf_router_0_1's
BGP stanza — `neighbor 172.16.0.6 remote-as 65100` (toward spine_router_0_0)
and `neighbor 172.16.0.10 remote-as 65101` (toward spine_router_0_1) —
mirroring the working structure of leaf_router_0_0.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly lists the two missing neighbor statements (172.16.0.6 to spine_router_0_0 and 172.16.0.10 to spine_router_0_1) and cites `show bgp summary` showing no neighbors.
The remediation correctly instructs re-adding the two missing BGP neighbor statements on leaf_router_0_1 (or restarting FRR to reload /etc/frr/frr.conf), which restores the BGP sessions and routes.

The agent's investigation logs (running-config fetches, BGP summaries, and explicit agent notes) substantiate the core observation—leaf_router_0_1 has no BGP neighbor statements—and the writeup draws a direct, logical causal chain from that to the BGP sessions being down and the host isolation.
